title: Your updated training
intro: New games update what to practice. We recommend only patterns repeated across several games.
coverage: {{analyzed}} of {{eligible}} eligible games analyzed · {{decisions}} verified decisions
progress: Analyzing: {{done}} of {{total}} decisions. You can keep using the app.
empty: No recurring pattern has enough evidence yet. Import your games or update the analysis.
evidence: {{errors}} errors across {{games}} games · {{opportunities}} comparable decisions analyzed
causeUnknown: We know the context of these errors; we do not yet know their cause.
practiceEvidence: {{successes}} successes in {{independent}} first attempts without help · {{attempts}} total attempts

transferObserved: Errors per 100 comparable decisions: {{before}} before → {{after}} after. A descriptive comparison, not proof of a training effect.
method: Updates use verifiable rules, not neural network retraining. Up to 200 completed 10+0 games with confirmed identity are analyzed; very short games and special starting positions are excluded. A pattern requires errors across at least three games and three distinct positions. Only fully analyzed games count.
playNow: Your turn. Play directly on the board.
feedbackNote: The board shows your move and the opponent’s principal reply, when available. A valid alternative also counts.
assisted: This attempt is useful practice; it does not count as an independent first attempt.
demonstration: This is a reference move. Return to the starting position and play the idea.

errors.analysis_unverified: The analysis could not be verified. Progress is preserved; you can retry.
errors.analysis_failed: Analysis was interrupted. You can resume without losing verified decisions.
errors.engine_changed: The engine changed during analysis. Update to obtain comparable evidence.
errors.exercise_unavailable: This position is no longer available. Return to your patterns and choose another.
errors.insufficient_holdout_positions: We need at least two different positions from your games to practice and run an independent check. Import more games or update analysis.
errors.pattern_not_recurrent: There is not enough evidence to recommend this pattern yet.
errors.illegal_move: That move is illegal. Choose another.

piece-loss.title: Losing pieces
piece-loss.observation: After these moves, the opponent’s principal reply captures a piece and the evaluation worsens.
piece-loss.goal: Find a move that keeps your pieces safe.
piece-loss.hint: Look at pieces that would be undefended after moving and the opponent’s captures.
piece-loss.rule: Before committing to a move, inspect the opponent's checks, captures, and threats against your most exposed piece.
piece-loss.contrast: If no reply wins material or forces a concession, continue with your plan.

missed-capture.title: Missed valuable captures
missed-capture.observation: The engine found a piece capture better than your move in these positions.
missed-capture.goal: Look for a useful capture and check the opponent’s reply.
missed-capture.hint: Look for attacked enemy pieces. Before capturing, calculate the recapture.
missed-capture.rule: Before choosing a plan, inspect every capture and calculate first those that change material or force a reply.
missed-capture.contrast: An available capture is not automatically good: check the recapture and the resulting position.

missed-mate.title: Missed mating opportunities
missed-mate.observation: The engine found a forced mate, but your move did not preserve a verified mate.
missed-mate.goal: Look for a forcing continuation against the king.
missed-mate.hint: Look at checks and the king’s escape squares; calculate all legal replies.
missed-mate.rule: When the opposing king is exposed, calculate every check before evaluating quiet moves.
missed-mate.contrast: Reject a check if the king escapes or the line loses the attack; do not force a mate that is not there.

forcing-reply.title: Forcing replies by the opponent
forcing-reply.observation: The opponent’s principal reply gives check after these costly decisions.
forcing-reply.goal: Choose a move accounting for the opponent’s checks.
forcing-reply.hint: Before playing, imagine the opponent’s most uncomfortable check.
forcing-reply.rule: For every candidate, first imagine the most hostile reply: check, capture, or direct threat.
forcing-reply.contrast: Only after surviving that reply should you compare slower plans.

closed-center.title: Decisions in blocked centers
closed-center.observation: Several costly decisions occurred with at least two locked pawn pairs. No strategic cause was identified.
closed-center.goal: Improve your pieces or prepare a pawn break without weakening the position.
closed-center.hint: Look for lines you can open and a piece that needs improvement. Check threats before preparing your plan.
closed-center.rule: With a locked center, identify your pawn break and improve the pieces that must support it before attacking.
closed-center.contrast: If the opponent can open the center first or has an immediate threat, address it before preparing your break.

endgame-decisions.title: Decisions with few pieces
endgame-decisions.observation: Several costly decisions occurred in low-material positions. The technical cause is not yet identified.
endgame-decisions.goal: Look for a continuation that preserves your endgame options.
endgame-decisions.hint: Compare king activity, passed pawns and immediate threats before moving.
endgame-decisions.rule: In endgames, compare king activity, passed pawns, and immediate threats before calculating exchanges.
endgame-decisions.contrast: A favorable material trade can be poor if it leaves your king passive or creates an opposing passed pawn.

path.holdoutTitle: Find the decision without knowing the theme
path.holdoutGoal: This is another position from your games. There is no hint or label: decide what the position requires.
path.holdoutPrompt: Your turn. Think as you would in a real game and play without help.
path.holdoutRecorded: Result recorded as an independent check.
path.holdoutAssisted: This counts as practice, but not as an independent check.
path.acceptableReference: Your move is valid. {{move}} is another verified reference.
path.compareReference: Compare it with {{move}}, the verified reference in this position.

pedagogy.observed: I see {{errors}} errors in {{games}} games among {{opportunities}} comparable decisions.
pedagogy.unknown: That confirms an observable recurrence; it does not yet explain why it happens.
pedagogy.checking: I want to test a hypothesis from the previous session
pedagogy.stillTentative: It remains tentative until independent evidence appears in other positions and games.
pedagogy.coachQuestion: I want to understand how you were thinking
pedagogy.intentionLabel: What were you trying to achieve with your move?
pedagogy.evaluationLabel: How did you evaluate the position after the reply you expected?
pedagogy.explicitCost: Pedagogical analysis uses one bounded call only when you press this button. It is not repeated automatically.
pedagogy.rulesFallback: The pedagogical model is not configured. Your answer will be saved and you will receive a rule-based intervention.
pedagogy.confidence: Confidence: {{value}}. This is not yet a diagnosis.
pedagogy.llmSource: Synthesised from structured evidence; moves and variations come from the engine.
pedagogy.ruleSource: Provisional rule-based intervention; no model inference was made.

decision.title: Let’s understand your decision
decision.intro: Decide without hints first. Then we will examine the reply you expected and what to work on.
decision.choose: Choose your move on the board.
decision.replyPrompt: You chose {{move}}. Now play the opponent’s pieces: what is their strongest response?
decision.hypothesis: This is one observation, not a confirmed cause of your mistakes. We will check it in other positions.
decision.memory: We retain {{count}} recent decisions on this topic to compare your approach.

followup.search: Check what the opponent can do this time.
followup.compare: Look beyond the first reply you notice.
followup.evaluate: At the end of your calculation, decide who benefits.
followup.uncertain: Your prediction has not yet been verified.
followup.reinforce: Try to sustain your approach without help here.

search.title: Let’s work on finding replies
search.body: You proposed no response and your move lost value. The opponent has {{actual}}.
search.task: Return to “After my move”. Look for checks, captures and threats. Then inspect the reply and retry your decision.

compare.title: Your prediction missed a stronger defence
compare.body: You expected {{predicted}}. The engine verified that this reply concedes more than a strong defence; here it suggests {{actual}}.
compare.task: Compare the position after your move with the opponent’s reply. Identify what changes and retry with a candidate that withstands that defence.

evaluate.title: You saw a strong reply; let’s examine its consequences
evaluate.body: Your predicted {{predicted}} is a strong, valid response according to the engine, but your initial move loses value.
evaluate.task: Reconstruct your calculation. Compare material, king safety and activity at the end. Compare your candidate with the reference and retry: which consequence did you value differently?

uncertain.title: We cannot yet explain the difference
uncertain.body: Your move was verified, but the strength of your predicted response could not be verified.
uncertain.task: Inspect the opponent’s reply and compare it with your prediction. We will not attribute a cause without that check.

reinforce.title: Your decision keeps a valid continuation
reinforce.body: This time you chose a valid move. That does not yet demonstrate mastery.
reinforce.task: Continue the position. Keep considering the opponent’s response even when the plan changes.
